answer: Detect farms spectrally, not heuristically. Build the attestation graph, edge a to b when a attests b, take the normalised Laplacian and its Fiedler vector, then collapse each dense community into one voter weighted by its strongest member. A farm attests itself, so its identities sit in one community and N clones carry one vote. To hide, it must source every attestation from a distinct external non-kin attester, a finite pool priced by that attester's stake, so marginal cost per identity stays flat. The trellis keeps one ivory branch; the nectar is shared once.
